alerts.title: Carbamazepine co-administration may markedly lower dolutegravir levels
alerts.message: Guidance states carbamazepine decreases DTG levels by 30-70% and recommends using valproic acid instead as an anti-epileptic. This patient is on DTG with carbamazepine added 2 weeks ago alongside valproate. Viral load has risen from <50 copies/mL (2025-09-01) to 1,240 copies/mL today, and the timing fits the carbamazepine start, though adherence is reported good and other causes are not excluded.

evidence.recommended_action: Avoid carbamazepine with DTG; use valproic acid as the anti-epileptic per guideline. Repeat viral load in 2-3 months with enhanced adherence support, and consider genotype testing if viral load remains above threshold.

alerts.title: Detectable viral load on DTG-based regimen requires structured response
alerts.message: Guidance recommends that for VL above 50 copies/mL, clinicians provide enhanced adherence support, address side effects, repeat VL in 2-3 months and consider investigating causes. Current VL is 1,240 copies/mL, and the plan does not document these steps.

evidence.recommended_action: Provide enhanced adherence support, address side effects affecting adherence, repeat viral load in 2-3 months, and investigate for drug interaction or resistance if it remains elevated.

alerts.title: Hyponatraemia and neurotoxicity signs may be drug-related
alerts.message: Sodium is 128 mmol/L, with nystagmus, ataxia and tremor alongside carbamazepine level 14 mcg/mL (above range 4-12). Carbamazepine toxicity and valproate co-therapy can both contribute to hyponatraemia and neurological signs, and non-drug causes are not excluded in this assessment.

evidence.recommended_action: Review carbamazepine dosing urgently in line with the clinician plan, repeat level and sodium, and reassess neurological status; consider changing the anti-epileptic regimen given the DTG interaction.
